summary: Failure modes generated and agreement-checked from 300 traces.

codes.name: Context_Window_Capacity_Degradation
codes.description: The token budget available to an agent is exhausted or critically pressured — either on the input side (claim + retrieved passages + prior summaries approaching or exceeding the context window limit) or on the output side (generated content truncated mid-stream because the output buffer or remaining token allowance is depleted). Both input-pressure degradation and output truncation are manifestations of the same underlying resource constraint and are coded here.
codes.when_to_use: Apply when: (1) agent output is visibly incomplete, cut off mid-sentence, or mid-reasoning; (2) quality of reasoning degrades noticeably as input length increases; (3) earlier retrieved content appears to be ignored or forgotten in later output; (4) pipeline logs show token counts approaching or exceeding model limits; (5) summarize->create_query handoff passes an unusually large combined payload.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do NOT apply when output is incomplete due to a system-level runtime error (use A.14) or when the agent explicitly refuses to respond without any token pressure evidence (use A.12). Do not apply when repetitive looping is observed without corroborating evidence of token pressure (use A.3 alone in that case).

codes.name: Repetitive_Looping_Output
codes.description: An agent produces output containing repeated phrases, sentences, paragraphs, or reasoning blocks, indicating the generation process has entered a degenerate loop rather than progressing toward task completion. May occur due to sampling instability, model-level attention degradation, or as a downstream symptom of context window pressure (A.1). When context pressure is the likely cause, A.1 is the primary code and A.3 is applied as a secondary symptom tag; when looping occurs without evidence of context pressure, A.3 is applied as the sole code.
codes.when_to_use: Apply as the primary code when repeated content is observed and there is no corroborating evidence of token budget pressure (input length is well within limits, no truncation signals). Apply as a secondary code alongside A.1 when repetition occurs in the presence of long inputs or documented context pressure.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do NOT apply when apparent repetition is intentional (e.g., structured recaps, bullet reformatting). Do not apply when output is merely verbose or redundant in reasoning style without true looping patterns. Do not use as the sole primary code when token pressure evidence is present — elevate A.1 to primary in that case.

codes.name: Instruction_Non_Compliance
codes.description: An agent ignores, misinterprets, or only partially follows its system prompt or task-specific instructions, producing output that does not conform to the expected format, scope, or behavioral constraints. Includes cases where required output fields are omitted, prohibited behaviors are performed, output language or structure deviates from specification, or task scope boundaries are violated.
codes.when_to_use: Apply when agent output can be directly compared to explicit instructions and a deviation is observable — wrong format, missing required fields, out-of-scope content, violated constraints, or wrong output language.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do NOT apply when deviation is caused by a system-level error interrupting execution (use A.14), by token exhaustion truncating output before completion (use A.1), or by the agent explicitly refusing (use A.12). Do not apply when instructions were themselves ambiguous and the agent produced a reasonable interpretation.

codes.name: Agent_Refusal_Or_Abandonment
codes.description: An agent declines to produce a substantive response to its assigned task through model-driven or prompt-driven non-response — outputting an empty string, a meta-comment about inability to answer, an unsolicited deferral, or an unexplained blank output — without any detectable system-level error signal. This code covers non-response that originates from the model's own behavior, not from infrastructure failure.
codes.when_to_use: Apply when an agent produces no usable output and there is no accompanying system error log, API exception, or runtime failure signal. The non-response appears to originate from the model itself (safety filter, perceived impossibility, misrouted task, or model instability).
codes.when_not_to_use: Do NOT apply when a system-level error log, API error code, exception trace, or network failure message is present — use A.14 instead. Do not apply when output is merely very short but substantive. Do not apply when truncation (A.1) explains the missing content.

codes.name: Runtime_Execution_Error
codes.description: A system-level, infrastructure-level, or API-level error occurs during agent execution that interrupts normal processing and prevents the agent from producing usable output. Includes API errors, HTTP error responses, runtime exceptions, network failures, timeout events, and memory errors other than context-window overflow. The defining characteristic is the presence of a detectable error signal in logs or the pipeline response — distinguishing it from model-driven non-response (A.12). Note: the downstream observable symptom of this code (missing or empty output) may superficially resemble A.12; apply A.14 whenever an error signal is present.
codes.when_to_use: Apply when execution is interrupted by a detectable system-level signal: an exception trace, a non-2xx HTTP status code, a timeout event, a memory error, or an API error message. Use A.14 regardless of whether the downstream symptom looks like a refusal, as long as the error signal is present.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do NOT apply for context-window token exhaustion resulting in truncated output (use A.1). Do not apply when the model produces an empty or refusal response with no error signal (use A.12). Do not apply for output quality failures that have no associated system error (use the appropriate quality-degradation code).

codes.name: Coordinator_Asymmetric_Summary_Weighting
codes.description: The coordinator disproportionately incorporates conclusions from one summary while effectively ignoring the other, producing a query that reflects only one summarizer's analysis despite both being available inputs, resulting in a systematically biased retrieval direction.
codes.when_to_use: When the two summaries offer different but non-contradictory perspectives or cover different aspects of the claim, and the output query reflects only the framing or findings of one of them, discarding useful signal from the other.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the summaries are so similar in content that using either one produces the same query. When one summary is clearly more relevant to the unresolved question and selective use is appropriate.

codes.name: Coordinator_False_Claim_Verification_Acceptance
codes.description: The coordinator accepts a summary's claim of verification without scrutiny when the summary's own reasoning reveals the evidence is incomplete, mismatched, or only partially supportive, then generates a query premised on the claim being true rather than seeking confirming or disconfirming evidence.
codes.when_to_use: When a summary states the claim is 'verified' or 'supported' but the summary body itself notes caveats, missing evidence, or only partial confirmation, and the output query proceeds as if full verification occurred.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the summary's verification is internally consistent and well-supported by passage citations. When partial verification is sufficient context to generate a useful follow-up query.

codes.name: Coordinator_Failure_To_Reconcile_Contradictory_Summaries
codes.description: When summary_1 and summary_2 provide contradictory assessments of the same sub-claim, the coordinator generates a query that ignores or papers over the contradiction rather than targeting the specific point of disagreement for resolution.
codes.when_to_use: When summary_1 and summary_2 disagree on a factual point (one says supported, the other says unsupported or gives conflicting detail) and the subsequent query does not address the specific disputed fact.
codes.when_not_to_use: When both summaries agree, or when the query explicitly targets the disputed fact between the two summaries.

codes.name: Coordinator_Misidentifies_Critical_Unverified_Sub_Claim
codes.description: The coordinator fails to route the hop-3 query toward the most consequential unverified sub-claim identified in the summaries, instead targeting a peripheral or secondary aspect, leaving the highest-risk factual gap unaddressed.
codes.when_to_use: When one or both summaries explicitly flag multiple unverified sub-claims and the hop-3 query targets a lower-stakes sub-claim while ignoring the higher-stakes one.
codes.when_not_to_use: When only one gap exists or when the query correctly targets the most critical gap identified in the summaries.

codes.name: Wrong_Year_Or_Date_Accepted
codes.description: The reasoning accepts or fails to challenge an incorrect year or date in a claim, even when the retrieved passages contain a contradicting year or date that is visible in the trace.
codes.when_to_use: When a claim states a year/date (e.g., 'founded in 1976', 'starting in 1982') and the retrieved passages visible in the trace state a different year/date, but the summary treats the claim's year as correct or does not flag the discrepancy.
codes.when_not_to_use: When no passage in the trace contains a year that contradicts the claim. Do not apply when the date discrepancy is acknowledged and correctly flagged as unsupported.

codes.name: Hallucinated_Passage_Support
codes.description: A summary asserts that a passage confirms or contains a specific fact that the passage does not actually state, effectively fabricating evidence for the claim.
codes.when_to_use: When a summary attributes a specific fact to a numbered passage (e.g., 'passage 1 identifies X') but the passage text visible in the trace does not contain that fact or contains contradicting information.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the summary's assertion is genuinely supported by the passage text shown in the trace, even if the overall reasoning is flawed for other reasons.

codes.name: Absence_Of_Evidence_Treated_As_Evidence_Of_Absence
codes.description: The reasoning concludes that a claim is false or unsupported because passages do not mention a fact, when the passages simply do not address that fact at all — treating silence as contradiction.
codes.when_to_use: When a summary concludes that sub-claim X 'does not' hold or is 'false' solely because no passage mentions it, without any passage affirmatively contradicting it.
codes.when_not_to_use: When a passage explicitly states something that contradicts the claim, making the 'not supported' conclusion evidence-based rather than inference-from-silence.

codes.name: Intermediate_Entity_Identification_Failure
codes.description: In a multi-hop chain, the reasoning fails to correctly identify or resolve the intermediate entity (the bridge between two facts), causing the entire chain to be unverifiable or verified against the wrong entity.
codes.when_to_use: When a claim requires first identifying entity A from a description, then verifying a fact about A, but the reasoning either misidentifies A or proceeds without confirming A's identity, leading to verification of a different entity's facts.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the intermediate entity is correctly identified in the first hop and the failure lies elsewhere in the reasoning chain.

codes.name: Contradictory_Evidence_Ignored_In_Verdict
codes.description: A retrieved passage explicitly contradicts the claim, but the summary or final verdict ignores or minimizes this contradiction rather than marking the claim as not supported.
codes.when_to_use: When passage text in the trace directly states something that contradicts the claim (e.g., establishment date differs, different monarch named), but the summary still leans toward 'supported' or 'partially supported' instead of 'not supported'.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the contradiction is correctly identified and the verdict is appropriately 'not supported' or 'false'.

codes.name: Entity_Substitution_Undetected
codes.description: The reasoning attributes facts from one entity to a different but related entity (e.g., confusing two members of the same band, two composers of similar works, two people with the same surname), and the substitution is not detected despite passages in the trace containing disambiguating information.
codes.when_to_use: When the passages in the trace describe entity A (e.g., the correct bass guitarist, the correct composer) but the summary or verdict applies those facts to entity B named in the claim, without noting the distinction.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the passages do not contain enough information to distinguish the two entities. Do not apply when the correct entity is genuinely ambiguous in the retrieved evidence.

codes.name: Unsupported_Superlative_Accepted
codes.description: The reasoning accepts or does not challenge a superlative or comparative assertion in the claim (e.g., 'largest', 'first', 'only', 'most durable') without any retrieved passage explicitly confirming that ranking or uniqueness.
codes.when_to_use: When a claim contains a superlative/comparative (e.g., 'the first Russian composer', 'the largest defined region') and no passage in the trace explicitly confirms that ranking, yet the verdict is 'supported' or the summary treats it as verified.
codes.when_not_to_use: When a passage in the trace explicitly states the superlative (e.g., 'was the first Russian composer whose music made a lasting impression internationally'). Do not apply when the ranking is directly confirmed by passage text.

codes.name: Category_Or_Count_Mislabel_Accepted
codes.description: The reasoning accepts or fails to flag a mislabeled category, type, or count in the claim (e.g., 'three-act play' when passages say two acts; 'Indian language' when passages describe a religion; 'words' when passages describe saints) despite passage evidence to the contrary being visible in the trace.
codes.when_to_use: When a claim uses a categorical label or count and the retrieved passages visible in the trace contradict that label or count, but the summary treats the claim as correct.
codes.when_not_to_use: When no passage in the trace addresses the category or count in question. Do not apply when the mismatch is correctly flagged as unsupported.

codes.name: Partial_Verification_Treated_As_Full
codes.description: A compound claim containing multiple distinct sub-claims is marked as fully supported after only a subset of those sub-claims are verified, with remaining sub-claims either unaddressed or explicitly flagged as unverified in the trace.
codes.when_to_use: When the summary explicitly acknowledges that one sub-claim cannot be verified (e.g., 'the passages do not contain information about X') but the overall verdict is still 'supported' or the trace proceeds as if the claim is resolved.
codes.when_not_to_use: When all sub-claims in the compound claim are addressed by retrieved passages, even if some are only partially supported. Do not apply when the unverified sub-claim is trivially implicit from the verified ones.

codes.name: Contradictory_Sub_Summaries_Not_Reconciled
codes.description: Two summaries produced from the same evidence reach opposite conclusions on a key factual sub-claim (one says supported, the other says not supported or identifies different facts), and this contradiction is not resolved before a verdict is rendered or the next query is generated.
codes.when_to_use: When summary_1 and summary_2 are both visible in the trace and they explicitly contradict each other on a specific factual point (e.g., one names passage 1 as identifying entity A, the other says entity B), and no reconciliation step is taken.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the two summaries differ only in phrasing or emphasis but agree on the core factual conclusion. Do not apply when one summary simply has less detail than the other without contradicting it.

codes.name: Claim_Referent_Ambiguity_Unresolved
codes.description: The claim contains an ambiguous referent (e.g., 'this province', 'the other company', 'its founder') and the reasoning proceeds to verify facts without first resolving which specific entity the referent denotes, potentially applying evidence to the wrong entity.
codes.when_to_use: When a claim uses a pronoun or vague descriptor instead of a proper name, and the summaries or queries apply retrieved evidence without first explicitly resolving what entity the referent points to.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the referent is unambiguous in context (e.g., only one entity of that type exists in the passages) or when the trace explicitly resolves the referent before proceeding.

codes.name: Negation_Or_Logical_Scope_Mishandled
codes.description: The reasoning fails to correctly handle the logical structure of a claim that involves negation, disjunction, or a 'not both' / 'neither' construction, leading to an incorrect verdict about whether the claim is supported or refuted.
codes.when_to_use: When the claim uses negation or a compound logical form (e.g., 'are not both located in X', 'neither A nor B') and the summary either ignores the negation or verifies the wrong logical condition.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the logical structure is a simple positive assertion. Do not apply when the negation is correctly handled and the verdict properly reflects the logical form of the claim.

codes.name: Geographic_Location_Misattribution
codes.description: The reasoning incorrectly assigns a geographic attribute (city, region, country) to an entity, accepting a wrong location as correct or failing to detect a location mismatch between the claim and the evidence.
codes.when_to_use: When a summary states or accepts a geographic claim (e.g., 'located in Bavaria') that contradicts passage text (e.g., 'located in Weimar'), without flagging the discrepancy.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the geographic error is in the original claim and is correctly identified as an error by the summaries.
